clue.text: Spooner's departed newspaper — Standard for The Socialist?

indicators.note: the apostrophe-s points to Reverend Spooner, so the opening sounds of the two words swap places

parts.note: someone who departed fled
rag is a dismissive word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A defunct socialist paper is offered as the movement's standard.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening FL and R of FLED RAG gives RED FLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The banner of socialism is a crimson flag, and a standard is a flag carried as an emblem.

clue.text: English label put on before for furniture item

parts.note: a tag is a label
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A furniture maker attaches an English label to a piece before sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot with open shelves for displaying ornaments, a French-named piece of furniture.

clue.text: Tailless dog buries long-necked creature that's smelling bad

indicators.note: the shortened dog's name surrounds the creature, burying it inside
a tailless word loses its last letter, here the dog's name is cut short

parts.note: Fido is a stock name for a dog
E.T., the film alien, has a famously long extendable neck

explanation.surface: A stumpy-tailed dog digs a hole to bury a giraffe-like animal that reeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' leaves FID; 'buries' needs the film alien, whose stretchy neck is the joke, placed after the first letter. 'Long-necked creature' tempts toward giraffe.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetid is a synonym for stinking or foul-smelling.

clue.text: Current tester came across fracture, finally, in broken arm

indicators.note: the met-plus-letter group is placed inside the scrambled arm
a broken arm is a damaged one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to come across someone is to have met them

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of fracture

explanation.surface: A doctor discovers a fracture in a broken arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns ARM into AMR, which holds MET plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument measuring electric current in amperes, hence a tester of current.

clue.text: Thief caught by tackle is wounded — stretcher produced?

indicators.note: the thief is held inside the scrambled letters, as if caught
wounded means damaged, so the letters of tackle is are rearranged

parts.note: a nicker is one who nicks, a thief

explanation.surface: A thief tackled and hurt in the process ends up being carried off on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wounded' rearranges 'tackle is' to give the K and the second word; 'caught by' places the thief between them. Knicker elastic is the waistband of British underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Elasticated waistband in underwear is a made stretchy product, a manufactured stretcher.

clue.text: Hose only used between poles

indicators.note: the scrambled word sits between the two poles

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: used suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hosepipe is only to be used between two posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are stockings, and hose is an old word for stockings or tights.

clue.text: Clear quality is overcoming limits of production in plant

indicators.note: the inner group is placed in the name of the plant

parts.note: cress is a salad plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, is placed over the next letters sits on top of them
limits are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of production

explanation.surface: A clear quality wins out over the limits of production at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' stacks the first piece above the PN from 'limits of production', and 'in' puts that group inside the salad plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Crispness is clarity or sharpness, as of a picture or sound.

clue.text: Old US lawman has to carry silencer

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous Wild West marshal
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A Wild West marshal has to carry a silencer on his gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug for the ear blocks out noise, so it silences sound for the wearer.

clue.text: Processed food, or the meat, going all the way down

indicators.note: processed food is altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Processed food or meat is described as passing right through the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means over the whole body, top to bottom, so all the way down.

clue.text: See 25
Principled strength in which Blair, for me, questionable

indicators.note: something questionable is doubtful or unsound, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A political commentator doubts that Tony Blair has principles.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was the British Labour prime minister from 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the inner integrity and resolve that keep someone principled.

clue.text: Good old penny in change — isn't that funny?

indicators.note: the penny is placed inside the word for change

parts.note: to edit is to change
D was the symbol for the old British penny, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: Someone finds a good old penny in their change and asks if that is funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang spelling of 'get it?', said after a joke to check the listener understood.

clue.text: Game of which day old parrot spoke

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: spoke says the parrot's name is heard, then spelt differently

parts.note: Polly is the stock name for a pet parrot

explanation.surface: An old parrot talked one day about a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known property-trading board game.

clue.text: Outdoor cafeteria guaranteed less posh cooking

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being prepared and mixed up
less signals letters taken away from the word

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, so posh

explanation.surface: A guaranteed meal, the cooking less refined, at an open-air restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U from GUARANTEED and rearrange GARANTEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden where refreshments are served outside, an open-air café.

clue.text: Information on foreign country's intimate parts

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Italia is the Italian name for Italy, so the country as foreigners call it

explanation.surface: Information about a foreign country's private matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The reproductive organs, a body's private parts.

clue.text: Tall girl's back covered in yellow and white?

indicators.note: back picks the last letter of girl's word

parts.note: egg has yellow yolk and white albumen, so this means smeared with egg

explanation.surface: A tall girl's back is splattered with something yellow and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Leggy describes someone with long legs, hence tall.

clue.text: View viewed, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: something viewed has been seen

explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a view, as of a landscape.

clue.text: Gap in line standing for disease

indicators.note: the gap goes inside the reversed line
standing up in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
a hole is a gap

explanation.surface: A gap in a line of people waiting for a disease test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns the curve upward to CRA in this down clue; 'in' places the gap within it, after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe bacterial infection of the intestine spread by dirty water.

clue.text: Letters are dealt with

definitions.meaning: letters are marked with where they should go, the wry reading
a problem dealt with has been tackled

explanation.definitionFit: To address an issue is to tackle it; envelopes carry a delivery destination written on them.

clue.text: Agent isn't getting to touch something up?

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
ain't is slang for isn't

explanation.surface: An agent is not allowed to touch anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a fresh coat of colour is to touch it up.

clue.text: See 5
Priest requiring silence before a prophet

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: A priest asks for silence before a prophet speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha was an Old Testament prophet, successor to Elijah.

clue.text: Iberian drink and Indian potato for the ladies on the move, perhaps

definitions.text: for the ladies on the move, perhaps

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
aloo is the Hindi word for potato, as in aloo gobi

explanation.surface: A menu of Portuguese wine and Indian potatoes for travelling ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTALOO is a British brand name for a portable toilet; 'ladies' is the women's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable toilet, so a ladies' loo that can be moved from place to place.

clue.text: Prisoner secreted by friend from the dominant uprising

indicators.note: the prisoner is hidden away inside the friend

parts.note: pal is a friend
lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner hidden by a friend escapes during a revolt against those in power.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a plagal mode spans upward from the dominant note, describing that range.

clue.text: Left to feed dog, perhaps, breaking in pieces for pudding

indicators.note: the fed pet breaks into the word for in pieces

parts.note: apart means in pieces

indicators.note: the letter is fed into the pet

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Leftovers fed to the dog, broken into pieces for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to feed' puts L into the pet to make PLET; 'breaking' splits the word for in pieces after its second letter. In Britain 'pudding' means any dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pastry dessert, a type of pudding in British usage.

clue.text: Madoff, for example, consumed by endless capital, as controversial multi-millionaire

indicators.note: consumed means eaten, so these letters are swallowed inside
endless removes the final letter of the capital

parts.note: Berlin is the German capital
Bernie Madoff was an American fraudster, so a US con man

explanation.surface: A notorious fraudster is swallowed by a city, as a disputed tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: BERLIN loses N to give BERLI, which holds US CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Silvio Berlusconi, the Italian media tycoon and prime minister dogged by scandal.

clue.text: Head for the starter

definitions.meaning: an old word for the top of the head
pâté is a meat paste often served as a first course

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the crown of the skull, and a savoury paste eaten as an appetiser.

clue.text: Plant with aromatic seeds, as garage empty?

definitions.meaning: an umbelliferous herb whose seeds flavour bread and cake
a garage is empty when the vehicle is out

explanation.definitionFit: A herb grown for its fragrant seeds; read in two words it says the vehicle is out.

clue.text: Temperature found in simian, one dead

indicators.note: the temperature letter is found inside the ape

parts.note: an ape is a simian
an ace is one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A temperature is taken on a monkey that has died.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism for dead, as in resting peacefully.
